stem: Why can a root zone remain physiologically stressed even when water and mineral nutrients are abundant?
choices: Excess water can reduce gas-filled pore space and limit oxygen diffusion to roots even when moisture and nutrients remain abundant
High nutrient concentration can replace the need for root-zone oxygen because dissolved ions supply the energy needed for respiration
Wet media can prevent mineral nutrients from dissolving, so the main stress comes from reduced nutrient availability rather than aeration
High moisture usually suppresses root respiration enough that oxygen supply becomes less important until the media begins drying
rationale: Roots require oxygen for respiration. When pores remain water-filled for too long, gas exchange and oxygen diffusion can become limiting even when water and nutrients are present.
